about.title: Whittier Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet entryway at a market off Whittier Boulevard. A cracked walkway outside an apartment near Painter Avenue. A loose handrail in a parking structure by Lambert Road. Falls like these happen quietly in Whittier, and the people who get hurt often blame themselves first. Property owners and the businesses that lease from them owe visitors a reasonable level of care, which means inspecting for hazards, fixing what they find, and warning about what they cannot fix right away. The hard part in most Whittier premises cases is proving notice: that the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the condition before you fell. Photos, incident reports, witness names, and a written request to preserve store surveillance video can make the difference between a claim that holds together and one that stalls. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Whittier residents with an independent attorney who handles premises liability claims on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Whittier Residents Use LawProactive for Premises Claims

items.title: Notice Is the Whole Case
items.desc: California requires you to show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and did not fix it or warn you. The attorneys in our network know how to build that proof from maintenance logs, inspection schedules, and prior complaints.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Whittier stores and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. An attorney can send a preservation demand early so the recording of your fall is not lost.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible, with your recovery reduced by your share. The two-year filing deadline still applies, and it is shorter when a public entity is involved.

items.question: I fell on a sidewalk in Whittier. Is the city responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who owns and maintains that stretch of sidewalk and whether the defect was one they knew or should have known about. Claims against the City of Whittier, Los Angeles County, or another public entity follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, generally requiring a government claim within six months. An attorney can help identify the responsible party quickly so no deadline slips by.

items.question: The store manager said I should have been watching where I was going. Do I still have a case?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California uses pure comparative fault, so even if a jury decided you were partly careless, you could still recover the portion attributable to the owner's negligence. Owners often raise this argument early to discourage people from pursuing a claim, which is one reason it helps to speak with an attorney before giving a recorded statement.
